newsitem.title: JAPAN: NTT says wants to provide one-stop billing service.
newsitem.headline: NTT says wants to provide one-stop billing service.

text.p: Nippon Telegraph and Telephone Corp is talking with the telecommunications ministry on the possibility of providing Japanese multinationals with a "one-stop" service under which they would pay local, long-distance and international bills to one service provider.
"There is a demand from Japanese multinationals abroad for a low-cost and reliable 'one-stop shopping service'," said NTT's senior executive vice president, Keiji Tachikawa.
"We hope to build communications networks for them by leasing lines, making it the first step in our international business," he said.

He said some form of tie-up with its international competitors, such as Concert planned by British Telecommunications PLC and MCI, and World Partners led by AT&T Corp, may be required to extend NTT's service, but nothing has been decided yet.
Tachikawa also said NTT's possible international projects include infrastructure development and investment in telecommunications operators abroad.

NTT, which has so far been prohibited from offering international services, said on Wednesday that it may announce its international business plans as early as January, following a recent agreement with the ministry on its corporate structure.
